chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al-Hannat, from Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A person in Ihram deliberately kills a bird between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the ransom, and the penalty, and he will be reprimanded.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'But if he did it deliberately in the Ka'ba?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the ransom, and the penalty, and he will be lashed less than the Legal Penalty (Hadd), and he will be stood before the people so that others may be deterred.'

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.كفارة: Expiation (implied by context of ransom/penalty in Ihram context)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for killing a bird while in Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the specific penalties for a muhrim who deliberately kills a bird, distinguishing between general areas of the Haram and the precincts of the Ka'ba. In both instances, the offender must pay both the fidya (ransom for the bird) and the jaza’ (compensation), but the disciplinary response varies: a general reprimand (ta’zir) applies to the former, while a public lashing (dun al-hadd) is prescribed for the latter to serve as a deterrent (kinaya) for the community. This ruling underscores the heightened sanctity of the Ka'ba's immediate vicinity within Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al Hannar, from Humran Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘One in Ihraam kills a bird deliberately in what is between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the ransom, and the penalty, and he would be reprimanded’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘But his deed was done deliberately in the Kabah’. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is the ransom, and the penalty, and he would be lashed less than the Legal Penalty (Hadd), and he would be stood (in front of) the people, perhaps others would be deterred’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad al-Hannat from Humran ibn ‘A’yan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. ‘What is the law about a man, who intentionally kills a bird between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah, while in the state of Ihram?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes ransom, penalty and he must be reprimanded.’

I then asked, ‘What happens if one intentionally does it in al-Ka‘bah?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes ransom, penalty and reprimanding below hadd (a measure of legal physical punishment) in public sight to make it a lesson for the others.’”
